title: fix(objectql)!: a by-id delete whose driver removes nothing answers RECORD_NOT_FOUND and runs no after-delete work
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Ca1jJvsA1dHsPwMiQb

Fixes #35329

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill or doc page teaches what the engine's by-id delete answers for a row that is gone; the REST and batch doors already answered 404 for this case and do not change.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：两个操作同时删同一条记录时，后到的那一个现在明确得到"记录不存在"，不再为别人删掉的记录重复触发删除后的处理、汇总重算和实时通知；页面和接口上看到的结果不变。
- 为什么做：之前后到者会把"删除后"的一整套动作再跑一遍，汇总被多算一次、订阅方收到两条删除通知，而且它得到的答复取决于有没有配置删除前规则，前后不一致。
- 出错会怎样：只影响自动化代码里直接调用删除、且恰好与别人同时删同一条的那一次调用：它会收到"记录不存在"错误而不是"未删除"，需要把这当作"已经被删掉"处理；最坏情况是某个自动化步骤因此报错停下，回滚只需撤回本次合并。
- 要你做什么：无，席位落地。

## 席位核对
### What changes

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, by-id branch, inside `runByIdDelete`: once the pre-image proved the row present (`:479`, unchanged), a driver answer of `false` from `driver.delete` (`:672`) now throws `recordNotFoundError(object, id, ctx)` (`:713`), the same error the pre-image miss throws, so `afterDelete`, the secret release, the roll-up recompute and `data.record.deleted` never run for it.
- Round 2 (contract review S1, route (a)): a child delete that a parent's cascade issued (`referentialCascadeDelete`, the claim decided once at `:215`) does NOT throw on that `false`. It sets `cascadeChildVanished` (`:710`) and returns `false`; right after the unit, `if (cascadeChildVanished) return result;` (`:743`) skips every after-effect, as for the refusal. The walk goes on and the parent's delete completes, which is `main`'s outcome for the parent. The decision is taken at the changed line, by the cascade claim only; the walk does not tolerate `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` in general.
- The throw sits after the recycle-bin `withdraw()` and outside the `try` whose `catch` calls `compensate()`, so the #31630 handling is what it was: the entry is written, then withdrawn, and never compensated a second time. It sits inside the unit (`this.transaction(...)` on the `atomic` plan), so a cascade the delete walked for a row it did not remove rolls back with it (#7413).
- An off-contract `0` is untouched (still passed through, entry still withdrawn). The predicate (many-row) path is untouched.
- Round 2 (N1), prose only: `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:468-478` (the pre-image is the first place to ask, not the only one; the driver's `false` is now read too), `:875-883` (`false` no longer reaches the result-shape check from the driver), `recycle-bin/capture.ts:172-180` (`withdraw()`: a later refusal's rollback takes the write and its withdrawal together), and the `capture.test.ts` cell title, now "logs at error, and still refuses with RECORD_NOT_FOUND, when the entry cannot be withdrawn".
- Clause-② measured on the diff: an engine caller that got the answer `false` for the delete it addressed now gets a refusal, so the arm is `no (narrowing)`, with a BREAKING section and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker in the changeset.
- Changeset (S1 + N2): states the cascade child's outcome; the stores are examples ("for example PostgreSQL ... and SQLite ..."); names the third door that already answered 404 (the own-row delete route, `own-row-delete-routes.ts:233`) and that the loser's `userMessage` there is now built by the engine from the route's system context, which carries no locale; the caller's fix says the error this change adds always names the row the caller addressed.

### Mechanism readings (A0-A3, round 1)

<details><summary>A0 — the four cells, measured (loser's answer · afterDelete · recompute · event)</summary>

Two writers delete one row; the first parks in a `beforeDelete` dispatch after its pre-image read, the second deletes meanwhile. Readings with the throw ablated (= `origin/main` behaviour) and with it in place:

| cell | without the fix | with the fix |
|:--|:--|:--|
| SQLite · no metadata hook | loser `false`; afterDelete ×2, recompute ×2, event ×2 | loser `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`/404; each ×1 |
| SQLite · metadata `beforeDelete` | second writer waits (unit holds the only connection), answers `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` at its pre-image; each ×1 | unchanged |
| PostgreSQL 16 · no metadata hook | loser `false`; each ×2 | loser `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`/404; each ×1 |
| PostgreSQL 16 · metadata `beforeDelete` | second writer does NOT wait; loser `false`; each ×2 | loser `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`/404; each ×1 |

So the hook-binding split the card describes is SQLite-only; on PostgreSQL the loser reached `false` under either binding. The PostgreSQL cells were a one-off measurement on a private temporary cluster, not committed.

</details>

- A2: withdraw first, then the throw, outside the compensating `try`. The #31630 pins in `recycle-bin/capture.test.ts` still assert `['create', 'delete']` on the bin and zero entries; only their expected answer moves from `false` to `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, and the transactional cell also asserts the cascade's contacts and note are back after the rollback.
- A3: there is no separate soft-delete branch in the engine; a recycle-bin delete is the same `driver.delete` call (plus the entry), so it reaches the same branch.

### Tests

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delete-driver-false-not-found-sqlite.test.ts` (round 1; real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` on better-sqlite3): the no-hook loser (`RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, each after-effect once, the winner's), the metadata-hook loser (serialised, same answer), CONTROL (a plain delete fires each effect once).
- `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.test.ts`: three `false` cells now assert the `{ code, status }` envelope (round 1); one title reworded (round 2).
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete.test.ts` (round 2):
  - "a delete of the very same row from inside the cascaded dispatch finds the token claimed" (`:1000`) is back to `main`'s outcome: the parent's delete resolves `true`, the parent and the child are gone. It also asserts the vanished cascade child ran no after-effect: `afterDelete` on the child fired once, from the hook's own (winning) delete, not marked as cascade-issued; `releaseSecretHandles`, `recomputeSummaries` and `publishDataEvent` were each called once for the child object (the winner's), not twice.
  - New CONTROL (`:1033`): the same self-deleting hook on a by-id delete the caller addressed still answers `{ code: 'RECORD_NOT_FOUND', status: 404 }`, with the same once-only after-effects.

<details><summary>Ablation, round 2 (new branch disabled via scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored to the HEAD blob)</summary>

At `ff325dcb26`, anchor `if (referentialCascadeDelete) {` replaced by `if (false as boolean) {`; objectql's test imports `./engine.js` from source, so no dist leg.

The cascade pin goes red; the CONTROL (the 1 passed) stays green.

</details>

<details><summary>Suites and typecheck, round 2</summary>

Every run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, verdict `command-exit 0` unless stated.

`ff325dcb26` carried a TS7006 (`Parameter 'args' implicitly has an 'any' type`) in the new spy filter, `engine-cascade-delete.test.ts:996`, which `check:test-typecheck` reports as an ARRIVED signature; `a6ec895d8c` types the filter (`(args: unknown[])` over `{ mock: { calls: unknown[][] } }`) and the gate holds with no ledger change. Between `382d79aa98` and `a6ec895d8c` only that test file's types changed. `test:repo` was not run locally (declared to CI: `Test Core`).

</details>

### Acceptance notes

- A cascade-issued child delete whose driver answers `false` answers `false`, runs no after-effects, and the parent's delete completes (S1, route (a)). One walk now gives one outcome for a dependent removed after its read, in both shapes: the batched chunk's count already tolerated it.
- A cascade can still stop on a dependent with `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, as before; the addressed row is then kept. Not changed here.
- The loser's `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` is logged at `warn` by the delete's existing catch ("Delete operation failed"), like the pre-image miss.
- REST, batch and own-row delete doors: unchanged code and status. On the own-row door the loser's `userMessage` is now built by the engine from the door's system context (no locale).
- `Lint & Repo Gates` / `TypeScript Type Check` were red on `2d1c794629` because the run was cancelled by the next push (every lint lane `cancelled`); `ff325dcb26`'s `Type Check · workspace` red was the TS7006 above.
